nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_000
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What issues arise from the linear supply chain of single-use electronic devices in healthcare?
nodes.answer: The linear supply chain results in the depletion of natural resources and excessive generation of e-waste, creating an unsustainable production and consumption model.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the initial phase examine waste generation in the fashion supply chain?
nodes.answer: The initial phase conducts a comprehensive examination of waste generation by using Waste Flow Mapping (WFM) to understand waste dynamics across the entire supply chain.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_003
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What are the seven input parameters taken by the model from various life cycle stages in the garment production process?
nodes.answer: The model takes in seven input parameters from the life cycle stages of production, supply chain, and use. These include selecting a garment design from 10 options, choosing fibre content from nine options, and deciding on the season between winter and all seasons.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: What type of model did Kim et al. (2018) develop for flows optimization in a CLSC of the fashion industry?
nodes.answer: Kim et al. (2018) developed a deterministic model for flows optimization in a Closed-Loop Supply Chain (CLSC) of the fashion industry, addressing concerns about demand uncertainty of recycled garments.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the significance of closed supply chains in the Circular Economy (CE) model?
nodes.answer: Closed supply chains are a pillar of the CE model as they present a challenge for its development. The CE model involves all stages from design to recycling, thus requiring cooperation among producer organizations, users, waste management entities, and suppliers of raw materials.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the challenges in redesigning the supply chain for the Circular Economy according to Bressanelli et al. (2019)?
nodes.answer: The challenges in redesigning the supply chain for the Circular Economy include issues such as reverse logistics, waste management, and material recovery.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_007
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How does Petersen and Ginsberg propose to develop a circular system for the acquisition and use of baby clothing?
nodes.answer: Petersen and Ginsberg suggest creating a system where parents can exchange or lease baby clothing instead of purchasing new items, promoting sustainability and reducing waste in the fashion industry.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_008
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What fields have successfully implemented the Best Worst Method (BWM)?
nodes.answer: The Best Worst Method (BWM) has been successfully implemented in fields such as manufacturing, sustainability, waste management, selection of supply chain partners, and green performance.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_009

nodes.answer: The Best Worst Method (BWM) has been successfully implemented in various fields such as manufacturing, sustainability, waste management, selection of supply chain partners, and green performance.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_010
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can Industry 4.0 and circular economy adoption barriers in the agriculture supply chain be identified?
nodes.answer: The ISM-ANP methodology can be utilized to identify Industry 4.0 and circular economy adoption barriers in the agriculture supply chain by analysing interrelations among various barriers and determining their priority for mitigation.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_011
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does Waste Flow Mapping (WFM) rely on quantitative data to optimize material flows in the fashion supply chain?
nodes.answer: Waste Flow Mapping (WFM) in the fashion supply chain relies on quantitative data to trace and optimize material flows. By using data, organizations can identify areas where waste is generated, accumulated, or moved inefficiently, allowing them to make informed decisions on waste reduction strategies and implement sustainable practices effectively.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_012
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What are some strategies for implementing circular business models in the textile and clothing industry?
nodes.answer: Some strategies for implementing circular business models in the textile and clothing industry include adopting sustainable sourcing practices, designing products for longevity and recallability, implementing take-back schemes for used products, and collaborating with stakeholders along the value chain to close the loop on materials and resources.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_013
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: What is the relationship between agility and product supply chain design in the case of the Swatch, as discussed in the Journal of Innovation Economics Management?
nodes.answer: The Journal of Innovation Economics Management discusses how agility impacts product supply chain design in the case of the Swatch, highlighting the need for flexibility and responsiveness in adapting to market changes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Circular supply chain management_qna_014
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: How did Tokugawa & Wong (2014) approach the development of a theory for multi-tier sustainable supply chains in their systematic literature review?
nodes.answer: Tokugawa & Wong (2014) conducted a systematic literature review to gather insights and information that would aid in the development of a theory for multi-tier sustainable supply chains.
